summary: The Safer Schools Act of 2025 establishes a five-year pilot program administered by the Attorney General to provide federal grants to public elementary and secondary schools. The grants are split into two categories: one to help schools pay for independent facility security risk assessments, and another to help them fund physical security improvements, such as video monitoring and silent panic alarms.

affected_groups.effect: Can apply for federal grants to conduct security risk assessments and make physical security improvements, subject to eligibility rules, reporting requirements, and matching fund obligations.

Will receive direct signals from newly installed school panic alarms and must provide written confirmation to schools regarding whether proposed security improvements mitigate identified vulnerabilities.
May experience altered physical school environments due to hard security improvements and will be surveyed one year later regarding their feelings of campus safety.

key_provisions: Establishes a DOJ pilot program for grants to public schools for independent facility security risk assessments.
Establishes a DOJ pilot program for grants to public schools to make hard security improvements identified by those risk assessments.
Requires schools applying for hard security grants to provide matching funds of up to 50 percent, subject to potential waivers based on financial need.
Mandates that if a panic alarm is not already installed or operable, hard security grant funds must be used to install at least one panic alarm directly linked to local law enforcement.
Gives priority in both grant categories to public schools that have experienced an event involving deadly harm or attempted deadly harm against multiple individuals.
Limits schools from receiving the same type of grant more than once every five fiscal years, except for schools that experience a multi-victim deadly harm event.
Authorizes appropriations totaling hundreds of millions of dollars over five years and sets up reporting requirements for grant recipients and the Attorney General.
missing_information: Exact total dollar amounts authorized for fiscal years three through five (the text mentions $300,000,000 for fiscal years three through five, but does not clarify if that is per year or total across those years).
Specific qualification criteria the Bureau of Justice Assistance will use to determine which entities can conduct independent facility security risk assessments.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Safer Schools Act of 2025 establishes a five-year pilot program administered by the Attorney General to provide federal grants to public elementary and secondary schools. The grants are split into two categories: one to help schools pay for independent facility security risk assessments, and another to help them fund physical security improvements, such as video monitoring and silent panic alarms.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a multi-year federal funding stream dedicated entirely to public school physical security and threat assessments, backed by authorized funding scaling up over five years and active oversight by the Department of Justice and Congress.

title: Safer Schools Act of 2025
